Hi Maya — thanks for the clear checklist. Quick answers and next steps:

- Invoice entity: Redwood will invoice from Redwood Inference, Inc. (US entity). If Stellix requires an EU invoice entity, we can discuss a localized invoicing arrangement (we'll need to confirm tax implications).

- Invoicing cadence: we can support split invoices by milestone. For the 3-milestone schedule you sent, finance prefers invoicing at 40% / 40% / 20% (with the final invoice released on acceptance). If Stellix needs the alternative schedule in your PDF, we can accept it but need to reconcile it with our revenue recognition team.

- Net terms: Standard is Net30. We can agree to Net45 for this deal on a one-off basis (given size and timing) if Stellix provides a PO and payment plan in advance. Alternatively we can offer Net30 with a 1% early-payment discount for Net15.

- Tax/withholding evidence: typical asks are tax residency certificate and a completed W-8/W-9 depending on entity. For EU VAT reverse charge, we'll need a valid VAT number and a statement from Stellix that reverse charge applies. Kimberly — can legal confirm the wording we should include in the Order Form re: withholding and gross-up?

I'll upload a tracked redline of the Order Form (minor commercial edits only) and the tax residency matrix to the thread shortly. Ben — can you confirm whether we can route the invoice to Redwood Inference, Inc. or whether we need the localized entity?

Maya / Rafael —

I reviewed Rafael's note and the attached Order Form redline. High-level legal summary of proposed changes we recommend to the Order Form to avoid back-and-forth at signing:

1) Invoice entity & remit-to: add explicit invoice remit-to clause naming Redwood Inference, Inc. as default invoicing party and include an optional Exhibit for alternate invoicing entity if Stellix requires an EU entity. Exhibit would capture legal name, tax id, and wiring instructions.

2) Payment cadence: preserve milestone split (40/40/20) as Rafael suggested but include language that final invoice is subject to acceptance criteria defined in Section 2.5. If Stellix's PDF proposes a materially different split, we add a brief carveout to allow bookkeeping alignment.

3) Net terms & early pay: accept Net45 as negotiated (commercial concession). Add an early-payment discount paragraph for Net30/Net15 where applicable.

4) Taxes & withholding: add clause that each party is responsible for its own taxes; where withholding applies under local law, the payer will withhold and provide certified evidence (tax certificate). Add Redwood's right to gross up if withholdings reduce the agreed consideration unless an alternate arrangement is agreed in writing.

5) Data for tax/VAT: request tax residency certificate, VAT ID (if EU), and completed tax form (W-8/W-9) prior to first invoice to prevent re-invoicing.

Action items for Stellix: provide the tax residency cert and indicate whether they require an EU invoiceable entity.

I attached a tracked Word redline (Stellix_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx) with the specific language. Note — we kept commercial edits conservative to avoid scope creep.
